subject: Request: Nova Integrations — bespoke availability concession & runbook
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Nova Integrations — bespoke availability concession & runbook

Quick summary: Nova (strategic, buying Dedicated + Private) is asking for a bespoke availability commitment tied to an operational runbook for their high-throughput inference paths. They want an effective p99 availability uplift (they phrased as "99.99 uptime equivalent for our critical routes") and explicit on-call/war room procedures. They understand this will be higher cost and are prepared to accept credits tied to missed targets.

Asks for this thread:
- Product: confirm whether we can commit to the runbook items below or whether alternate mitigations are required (cache warming, model variants, shorter token limits).
- Infra/Ops: feasibility of a geo-failover path + pre-warmed instances for peak windows and a rough delta in monthly committed spend.
- Sales: we need a recommended pricing uplift and list of non-negotiables.

Attached: nova_proposed_sla_draft_v1.pdf (customer-supplied), ops_runbook_checklist.xlsx (initial checklist from Nova).

Proposed next step: 1) Tech feasibility call today afternoon, 2) Draft concession terms to Legal after Ops sign-off.

— Alex

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Nova Integrations — bespoke availability concession & runbook

Thanks Alex — quick read of the attachments: Nova has called out 3 critical API routes (embed, rerank, chat-completion) that need the carveout. Ops checklist looks sensible but assumes warm standby in us-west + cold fallback to eu-west.

Product questions before we promise anything:
- Are we able to guarantee KV-prefix cache persistence across a failover without manual rehydration? If not, we should surface expected cold-cache latency and commit to a maximum recovery window rather than full behaviour equivalence.
- Can we limit the customer’s SLA to named routes + a TTL on long-context workloads? Long contexts blow up resource scheduling.

If Ops can scope the standby cost, I can propose a constrained SLA (named-route, p99 latency availability during business-hours, with explicit credit tiers).

Monica

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 13:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Nova Integrations — bespoke availability concession & runbook

Operational feasibility notes:
- Geo-failover (us-west -> eu-west) is doable but we cannot preserve GPU KV cache across regions. Recovery will require either: 1) prefix replay from customer (they have 1TB of warm prefixes in S3), or 2) background rehydration which adds 200–500ms on first-heavy requests.
- We can provide pre-warmed reserved capacity for their peak windows. Estimated incremental monthly cost: ~$45k for sustained pre-warmed pool sized for current forecasted load. Burst window (on-call activated) can spin up extra nodes but takes ~90s to reach full capacity unless we run them warm.
- Suggested mitigations: constrain the SLA to specific API routes and a per-route token limit. Add automatic fallback to a verified smaller variant when large contexts exceed TTL.

I'll join the tech call at 15:00 to walk the infra diagrams.

— Dev

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Nova Integrations — bespoke availability concession & runbook

Thanks — high-level commercial stance:
- We can offer a named-route availability concession if Product & Ops agree to the constrained scope (named routes + business-hours window + token limits).
- Pricing: recommend a 25% uplift on their committed Dedicated spend for the pre-warmed pool + a monthly ops surcharge of $12k for guaranteed standby shift coverage.
- Credits: tiered credits only for missed availability in-scope; exclude incidents caused by customer-side prefix replay or deliberate heavy context abuse.

If we can get Ops to confirm the $45k figure and Product accepts the route/TTL constraints, I will draft the commercial term (to be sent to Legal).

Aditya

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Lina Torres <lina@novaintegrations.com>, Jacob Ruiz <j.ruiz@novaops.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Nova Integrations — bespoke availability concession & runbook

Follow-up from tech call and exec alignment:
- Product sign-off: approved constrained SLA for named routes (embed, rerank, chat-completion) with a hard per-request token cap of 8k tokens; long-context traffic must be proxied to a non-SLA path.
- Ops sign-off: confirmed pre-warmed pool cost at ~$47k/mo (Dev updated estimate after factoring baseline headroom). Geo-failover accepted with caveat: first-wave cold penalty up to 500ms; we will document this and exclude it from credit triggers.
- Sales/Commercial: agree to 25% uplift and $12k ops surcharge; credits tiered as 10% credit for monthly downtime between 99.9–99.95, 25% credit below 99.9 for in-scope routes. Customer must accept a 30-day test period before full 12-month commitment.

Next steps (action owners):
- Alex: send updated SLA draft to Lina + link to runbook (today).
- Dev: produce the final runbook section on cache rehydration and fallback behaviour (EOD tomorrow).
- Monica/Product: draft the operational exclusions and telemetry conditions for credit triggers (send to Legal).
- Aditya: prepare commercial term sheet & provisional invoice for the uplift.

Lina/Jacob — thanks for patience; please confirm you accept the 30-day test and we'll get DocuSign going.

Evelyn
